name: FlexGen Power Systems, Inc.
employees: ~300–500 (2026, conflicting third-party estimates; no company figure published)
summary: FlexGen is a software-first battery energy storage integrator providing the HybridOS energy management system, engineering/integration, and lifecycle services for grid-scale storage. Founded in 2009 as a military hybrid-power hardware company (founder Josh Prueher), it pivoted to utility-scale storage integration and, after 2023, to a software-and-services model. In August 2025 it acquired the assets of bankrupt rival Powin ($36M stalking-horse bid: hardware/software IP, IT systems, spare parts), in April 2026 it acquired commissioning firm Clean Energy Services, and in June 2026 it launched European operations. Backed by Apollo Global Management ($150M, 2021), Vitol (anchored the $100M Series C, 2022), and Altira Group.
ecosystemRole: US-centric BESS integrator positioned around hardware-agnostic software and services rather than factory-built AC blocks: 25+ GWh across 200+ energy storage systems in 10+ countries under software and services after the Powin acquisition (company-reported). Historically claimed the #2 US storage-technology-provider spot and ~80% Texas share (2022, company claim, dated). Services the ex-Powin fleet and offers migration to HybridOS; European projects secured in the UK, Finland, and Sweden (2026).

productsAndServices.name: HybridOS Energy Management System (site controller + fleet management)
productsAndServices.description: Hardware-agnostic site-controls platform — EMS, site-level SCADA, and power plant controls — for grid-scale battery storage, sold in four control packages (ESS Block for non-exporting small sites, Storage for standard grid-interactive applications, Merchant for revenue-generating market participation with market-rule monitoring, Renewables for storage-plus-solar oversight). A fleet-management layer adds a multi-site dashboard with real-time dispatch and site/fleet-level charge-discharge scheduling. HybridOS v13 (Feb 2026) added a unified real-time/historical UI, a historian data API, a fleet-view mobile app, integrated market price access, predictive diagnostics with augmentation prediction, a charge-limit handler, and native CAN BMS support.
highlights: Control claims: 'fastest response times in the industry', unlimited application stacking, adaptation to any droop requirement (frequency, voltage, or power), and protection limits set at the point of interconnection (company marketing claims)
Integration record: 65+ hardware configurations from 22 global vendors over 15 years (company-reported)
'Works with any hardware that sends or receives a signal — whether it's a battery, solar array, wind turbine, cabinet door, or fire alarm' (company claim; no published OEM compatibility matrix)
productsAndServices.positioning: Independent, hardware-agnostic alternative to vertically integrated stacks: Tesla couples Autobidder/Opticaster optimization to Megapack hardware, and Fluence pairs its OS and Mosaic bidding software with its own AC blocks, while HybridOS is sold with no battery attached and controls any OEM's equipment. FlexGen competes for the controls/SCADA layer (against OEM-bundled EMSs and EPC in-house controls) rather than the AC-block supply that Wood Mackenzie's July 2026 global integrator ranking tracks (Sungrow, Tesla, CATL lead) — after the 2023–24 pivot FlexGen sells software and services, not batteries.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct licenses to storage owners, developers, IPPs, and utilities; bundled with FlexGen integration and commissioning; via the EMS Retrofit channel for takeovers of existing sites
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utility-scale storage owners/operators (US: ERCOT, CAISO, and other markets), data-center campuses, and — since June 2026 — European storage owners (UK, Finland, Sweden projects secured; staff in UK, Ireland, France, Spain, Poland)
productsAndServices.roadmap: DC-coupled control package listed 'coming soon' (2026); UL testing and VDE prototype certification in progress for German market entry (June 2026, company-reported)

productsAndServices.name: HybridOS Analyze
productsAndServices.description: Battery health and performance analytics module: field-measured state of health (SOH) and state of charge (SOC) across battery vendors, a digital-twin layer that learns site behavior for anomaly detection, and bottoms-up analysis of alarms, system events, and communication-network data with automatic retransmission of missed data.
highlights: Customizable alert thresholds with email notification; optimization recommendations for availability and battery balancing; underperformance and failure identification in near-real time
Automated monthly reporting, actual-vs-expected dashboards, warranty and compliance tracking
Feeds augmentation planning (v13 augmentation prediction) and the 24/7 Remote Operations Center when paired with lifecycle services
productsAndServices.positioning: Vendor-independent asset analytics versus OEM portals that cover only their own hardware; the digital-twin/anomaly-detection pitch parallels Fluence's Nispera-based analytics — FlexGen's angle is coupling the analytics to its own controls layer rather than selling analytics alone.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Subscription module alongside HybridOS EMS, or standalone for owner asset-management teams
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Asset managers and owner-operators of multi-vendor storage fleets

productsAndServices.name: HybridOS Control BMS
productsAndServices.description: US-engineered battery-management-system software layer governing cell balancing, thermal management, charge/discharge control, and fault protection, with cell- and module-level fault alerts and dynamic isolation of failing equipment while the rest of the site keeps operating; optimizes at block and site level rather than per battery.
highlights: Positioned on cybersecurity and supply-chain resilience: a domestic software layer between (typically foreign-made) battery hardware and site communications, with compliance updates independent of the hardware OEM
Claims support for numerous battery chemistries and manufacturer configurations; native CAN support added in HybridOS v13
productsAndServices.positioning: Addresses US regulatory and security concerns about foreign-origin BMS firmware without requiring hardware replacement — a lane with few US software competitors; no published cybersecurity certification list (IEC 62443 / NERC CIP not documented).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Sold with HybridOS EMS or as a retrofit layer on existing battery hardware
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utility-scale and C&I storage owners with domestic-content, cybersecurity, or compliance requirements

productsAndServices.name: Solar Power Plant Controller (PPC)
productsAndServices.description: HybridOS extension for hybrid solar-plus-storage plants — runs integrated with the EMS or independently on solar-only plants. v13 expanded it with native capacitor-bank control, solar shedding, meteorological-station inputs, solar-tracker management, and unified coordination of solar, storage, and substation assets.
productsAndServices.positioning: Extends the single-platform pitch to hybrid plants — one controller for storage and solar instead of separate PPC and EMS vendors.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Developers and owners of co-located solar-plus-storage and standalone PV plants

productsAndServices.name: EMS Retrofit
productsAndServices.description: Replacement of underperforming or orphaned third-party EMS/controls with HybridOS: vendor Modbus maps are used to model the site's DC and AC blocks, a digital twin simulates system behavior in FlexGen's Innovation Lab before any site work, then a field-tested 'one-touch commissioning' process swaps the controls with minimal downtime, followed by lifecycle services.
highlights: Claims 'the most seamless EMS transition process in the industry' with the majority of retrofit steps completed off-site (company claim)
Primary migration path for the ex-Powin fleet — HybridOS implementation fees waived for Powin customers who requested a retrofit within the Transition Services Period
productsAndServices.positioning: Monetizes integrator churn and bankruptcies (Powin 2025 is the flagship case) — competes with OEM re-controls offers and EPC in-house control swaps.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to owners of existing BESS sites
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Owners of sites with defunct, underperforming, or strategically risky EMS/controls vendors

productsAndServices.name: Integrated systems & data-center energy solutions
productsAndServices.description: Design, hardware-agnostic procurement across a global supplier network (with ITC/domestic-content compliance support), engineering studies and power modeling, construction support, and commissioning for grid-scale BESS — claiming '70% faster installations' via one-touch commissioning. The data-center offering positions campus-level BESS as the fastest path to power (deployment under one year versus 4–8-year grid interconnection queues), with grid-forming PCS for millisecond AI-workload swings, a site-level microgrid controller for grid-to-island transitions and black start, and 4-hour utility-scale batteries replacing conventional UPS.
highlights: BESSUPS (with Rosendin Electric, June 2025): medium-voltage (1–35 kV) utility-scale battery UPS replacement outside the data hall, combining Rosendin's BESSUPS design/method patent with FlexGen's Soft Grid Interconnection and Island Grid Transient Frequency Stabilization patents, grid-forming PCS, and HybridOS

Flagship references: ~2.15 GWh for Ameresco at three Southern California Edison substations on an emergency timeline (2021–22); 2 GWh for Vitol's VC Renewables; 10 GWh multi-year CATL supply agreement (2022); Hithium cooperation agreement (2023); Linxon collaboration
De-risking services: supply-chain management, regulatory compliance, and cybersecurity support
productsAndServices.positioning: Post-pivot FlexGen supplies no AC blocks of its own — integration is hardware-agnostic sourcing plus controls, versus factory-built block vendors (Tesla Megapack, Fluence, Sungrow PowerTitan) and EPC self-perform models.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct project contracts with developers, IPPs, utilities, and data-center builders; partner-delivered with EPCs (Rosendin) and equipment partners (Linxon)
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Storage developers/IPPs, utilities, government and industrial customers, AI data-center campuses

productsAndServices.name: Lifecycle services & remote operations
productsAndServices.description: 24/7 NERC-compliant Remote Operations Center in Durham, NC (plus subsidiary CES's Houston ROC): monitoring, root-cause analysis, field-service dispatch, preventative and corrective maintenance, spare-parts management housed at FlexGen's service center, warranty claim investigation with supplier coordination, augmentation management 'with nearly every hardware solution on the market', and contractual performance guarantees.
highlights: Availability economics: contractual 98% availability guarantee; 99% site-level availability claim when software is combined with lifecycle services; sites '22–49% above market average' revenue in ERCOT; 99.95% uptime through the 2021 Texas freeze; 1.6M hours of battery runtime (all company claims, not independently verified)

Clean Energy Services (acquired Apr 2026, operates as subsidiary): 125+ field technicians and engineers, 15+ GWh of BESS commissioned, 4.5+ GWh of battery sites and 1+ GW of solar under service, authorized-service-provider capability across major OEM platforms
productsAndServices.positioning: Availability-as-revenue pitch: unlike OEM long-term service agreements (Tesla, Fluence, Sungrow service their own fleets), FlexGen services any vendor's hardware — including orphaned fleets — and ties the service layer to HybridOS analytics.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term service agreements attached to HybridOS deployments and retrofits; standalone O&M and commissioning contracts via CES
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Owner-operators of utility-scale BESS and solar assets; data centers

productsAndServices.name: Powin fleet servicing & transition
productsAndServices.description: Continuity program for the ex-Powin installed base after FlexGen's Aug 2025 purchase of Powin's assets out of Chapter 11: hardware IP (the Centipede modular stacking platform, the Powin Pod 5 MWh 20-ft containerized BESS, spare-parts inventory), software IP (StackOS, Kobold), and IT systems. Transition Services Agreements kept Kobold access, AWS data storage, ROC services, and remote support running without disruption; former Powin staff were hired for operational continuity.
highlights: Migration path: customers retain Powin software initially, then EMS-retrofit to HybridOS — implementation fees waived within the transition window
The acquisition lifted FlexGen's supported base to 25+ GWh across 200+ systems in 10+ countries (company-reported)
productsAndServices.positioning: Turns a bankrupt hardware rival's fleet into a services annuity and a HybridOS retrofit pipeline — no comparable US offer at this scale for orphaned Powin sites.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct support/transition agreements with ex-Powin site owners (PowinSupport@FlexGen.com intake)
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Owners and operators of Powin Centipede and Pod sites

recentDevelopments.headline: Wood Mackenzie's first global BESS integrator ranking (Sungrow, Tesla, CATL on top) tracks AC-block suppliers — FlexGen absent from the hardware top-10
recentDevelopments.read: Confirms the lane FlexGen chose: it competes for the software/services layer on top of anyone's blocks, not for the block-supply share the ranking measures.

recentDevelopments.headline: Launched European operations — projects secured in the UK, Finland, and Sweden; staff in UK, Ireland, France, Spain, Poland; Germany in preparation (Mike Wallace, MD Europe)
recentDevelopments.read: First structural push beyond the US — software-and-services travels lighter than hardware, but needs local certification (UL testing and VDE prototype certification in progress).

recentDevelopments.headline: Acquired Clean Energy Services (Houston) — 125+ field technicians, 15+ GWh commissioned, 4.5+ GWh batteries and 1+ GW solar under service; terms not disclosed
recentDevelopments.read: Buys the field-service muscle that makes availability guarantees deliverable at fleet scale — commissioning and O&M capacity to match the software claims.

recentDevelopments.headline: HybridOS v13 released: unified real-time/historical UI, historian data API, fleet mobile app, market price access, predictive diagnostics with augmentation prediction, charge-limit handler, native CAN BMS support; solar PPC expanded
recentDevelopments.read: Moves the platform from control into prediction (diagnostics, augmentation forecasting) — the fleet-data moat argument for a software-first integrator.

recentDevelopments.headline: Completed $36M acquisition of Powin's assets out of Chapter 11 — Centipede/Pod hardware IP, StackOS and Kobold software IP, IT systems, spare parts; supported base now 25+ GWh / 200+ systems / 10+ countries
recentDevelopments.read: Fleet-in-a-box: an instant services annuity plus a captive EMS-retrofit pipeline, acquired without taking on a hardware manufacturing business.

recentDevelopments.headline: Partnered with Rosendin Electric on BESSUPS — medium-voltage utility-scale battery storage replacing conventional UPS infrastructure for data centers
recentDevelopments.read: The data-center wedge: BESS as both power quality and grid services outside the data hall, aimed at AI campuses stuck in interconnection queues.
